_comment: The real-photograph corpus. One entry per file in this directory.
Every image here arrived through WhatsApp: EXIF stripped, long edge 2048px,
0.02-0.11 bytes per pixel. That is the degradation photo_import_worker.py warns
about, and it is what destroys the Hungarian long umlauts. It is also, most
likely, how a congregation actually shares a song page - so treat this corpus as
the real distribution, not as a compromised one, and keep any future
camera-direct corpus in a sibling directory so the two can be compared.
tier: A = clean print, one column - must reach 100% and stay there.
B = the current frontier: two columns, italics, a second song on the page.
C = out of scope for the text path today; scored but excluded from the
headline number, because a handwritten chord written OVER a printed one
is an ambiguity no OCR setting resolves.
engine: which path the page is meant for - 'text' (browser Tesseract) or

pages.title: A mennyben fenn
pages.layout: single melody staff, chords above, verses 2-3 as prose below
stresses: the best notation case in the corpus: page pressed flat, no curl, good contrast
3/4 time and a metronome mark (quarter = 70) - Audiveris is known to report no time signature
slash chords: F/C, C/E, Am/G, C/G, F/G
lyrics are hyphenated per syllable under the staff, which Audiveris does not return at all
attribution lines (Ch. L. Bancroft, Ford.: Revesz Arpad, Vikki Cook) that are not lyrics
a printed page number (15) that is not a song number

pages.title: Van egy ut
pages.layout: single column, chord row above each lyric row
stresses: heavy show-through: the reverse page is legible mirrored across the whole sheet
PagePreprocessor show-through removal is the thing under test here
a parenthetical stage direction inside a lyric line: (vegen 3x)
an ellipsis joining two clauses: De hogyha ezen jarsz...Hazatalalsz!
G7 - a seventh spelled in full rather than as the -7 shorthand

pages.title: Szivemben orom dalol
stresses: the header of the NEXT song (99. Tobb erot) is on the page, cut off at the bottom edge
this is the 'a page holding two songs' warning case
chords are bold italic, not upright - a different glyph set to every other page here
lowercase minor: em, am
repeat marks as ASCII: //: and ://
a section label spelled Refr: rather than Refren
a trailing apostrophe inside a lyric: az en szivem'
a space before the period in the title line: 98 . Szivemben

pages.title: Kosz, jol vagyok
pages.layout: two columns; chords exist only in the left column, handwritten
stresses: every chord is handwritten in red marker and overlaps the printed lyric glyphs
the right column repeats the same verses with no chords at all
handwritten Hm is written as a struck-through H with a tail
the printed title reads Kosz where the first lyric line reads Kosz, jol erzem - title and first line differ
the page is inside a plastic sleeve: specular highlights and punch holes at the right edge

pages.title: Tart meg a kegyelem
pages.layout: single column, printed chords with a handwritten transposition written beside each
stresses: TWO competing chord sets on one page: printed (Dm, G7, B, A, Gm, A7, Asus4) and handwritten in blue pen a whole tone up (Em, A7, C, H, Am, H7, Hsus4)
which set the user wants is a product decision, not an OCR setting - this page is why tier C exists
printed chords use superscript quality: D with superscript m, A with superscript sus4, A with superscript 7
B in this book means B flat, and the handwritten C above it confirms the transposition - so the H-is-B rule must not fire on the printed B
stage directions inline with chords: - Intro x1, - Intro
verse 2 has no chord rows and must inherit verse 1 chords by line position (chord_carry.dart)
the header and first staff of song 110 (Te veled) are visible at the bottom edge

pages.title: Nincs mas Isten
pages.layout: two columns separated by a printed vertical rule; reading order is left column then right
stresses: a printed vertical rule between the columns - a gutter the column splitter can key on, unlike 166
named sections: 1. Versszak, 2. Versszak, Refren, Atvezeto resz
navigation lines that are not lyrics: -> Refren, -> Atvezeto resz, Vissza a versszakokra
an intro chord line with no lyric under it: Em7 Cadd9-Csus2 G5-Gsus2 D4/Fis
chord-only lines mid-song: Em C G D, C G D, C D G
Hungarian note-name spelling inside a chord: D4/Fis (F sharp)
compound chords joined by a hyphen: Cadd9-Csus2, G5-Gsus2
chords sit above the first word of a line rather than over a specific syllable

pages.title: Hozsanna
pages.layout: melody staff per system, chords above, syllabified lyrics below each system
stresses: the reverse page shows through across the upper half
the page curls into the spine at the right edge - the failure mode that takes 63 notes down to 6
four sharps in the key signature (E major / C sharp minor)
chords with Hungarian sharps: C#m, F#m7, G#m, E/G#, E/D#, and H meaning B natural
H4 as a suspended-fourth spelling
triplet brackets, repeat barlines, and the navigation marks Refr., Fine, D.S. and the segno
verse 1 and verse 2 are engraved as separate systems, so the same music appears twice
the last two systems have chords over empty (rest-only) bars

pages.title: Zengjed a dalt
pages.layout: single column, letterboxed inside a portrait screenshot
stresses: the photo occupies a band in the middle of the frame; black bars above and below
cropping to the page before reading is the thing under test
smallest file in the corpus at 0.021 bytes per pixel - the most compressed
the -7 shorthand meaning 'the chord before me, with a seventh'
lowercase minor: gm
a different book 151 to 151-hozsanna: the number is book-relative, not global
later verses carry no chords and must inherit them

pages.title: Tekozlo fiu
pages.layout: two columns with NO printed rule; the right column is italic, the left upright
stresses: no gutter rule and unequal column widths - the column splitter has only whitespace to go on
the right column is set in italic, the left is not, on the same page
the whole sheet is rotated a few degrees and lit unevenly from the left
extended chord qualities: Amaj7-A7, D-E
Hungarian lowercase minor spellings: dm, hm, fiszm (F sharp minor)
long runs of lyric lines with no chord row above them
a chord (D) in the right column sits past the right edge of the lyric line under it

pages.title: Jezus Krisztusom, mento oltalom
pages.layout: single column, large type, one verse
stresses: the song number 185 is handwritten in blue pen over the printed one
grey highlighter behind the title and behind the first lyric line
the 7 of H7 is struck through in pen twice - a correction that must not become a different chord
H7 must be read as B7 into storage
lowercase minor: em
two chords adjacent with one space: D G D
the verse ends in a four-dot ellipsis: halleluja ....
the largest type in the corpus - the easiest page, so a regression here means something basic broke

pages.title: Jezus szivedbe lat
pages.layout: screenshot of another song app: status bar, app bar, content card, navigation bar
stresses: born-digital glyphs, no paper, no skew, no show-through - the cleanest text case there is
phone chrome must be cropped away: a clock, a battery percentage and a title in the app bar
the app bar title duplicates the song title, which is a second source for it
chords are red and the lyrics black - colour is a usable signal here and nowhere else
no book number anywhere on the page: the number-out-of-the-title rule has nothing to split
chord runs joined by hyphens and wrapped in parentheses: G - C - D - ( C )
verses are numbered 1-4 in the lyric line itself
if this page is not read almost perfectly, the fault is in the bridge, not in the OCR
